name: get-member-self
description: Return the authenticated member's profile and team memberships.

name: get-automations
description: Get Release Autopilot settings: the account-wide auto-flagging and auto-releasing (the master gate a repository cannot exceed) and a page of repositories on the account's GitHub App install, each with mapped true or false and its project and effective settings when mapped. Mapped repositories not visible on the install are listed too, with visibleOnInstall false and no repo name. Pass repo (owner/name) or githubRepoId for one repository. Leave mapped unset to list connected and not-yet-connected repositories together; set it only when the user wants just one of the two groups. When hasMore is true, pass nextOffset as offset. When githubConnectUrl is present, GitHub is not connected: give that link to the user and retry after they finish. reposError means the install could not be read; retry later. section cleanup or archival with projectKey returns that project's auto-cleanup or auto-archival settings; an error saying automatic archival is not available means the account does not have it yet.

githubRepoId.description: Numeric GitHub repository id, an alternative to repo.

mapped.description: true lists only repositories mapped to a project; false only unmapped ones. Omit to list both.

offset.description: Pass nextOffset from the previous page.

projectKey.description: Any LaunchDarkly project key, used to look up the account-wide GitHub App install. Defaults to the oldest project.

repo.description: GitHub repository as owner/name, for example launchdarkly/gonfalon.

section.description: repos (default): account auto-flagging and auto-releasing and the repositories. cleanup: one project's auto-cleanup settings and the flags its next run picks up. archival: one project's auto-archival settings. cleanup and archival require projectKey.

name: update-automations
description: Update Automations settings: Release Autopilot auto-flagging and auto-releasing, and a project's auto-cleanup and auto-archival. One change per call. Account auto-flagging and auto-releasing: accountWide true. One repository: accountWide false with repo, and projectKey on the first map. A project's auto-cleanup or auto-archival: projectKey with a cleanup or archival object, and no repo. Saving cleanup makes the calling member the one whose permissions cleanup jobs use, and any schedule other than disabled makes LaunchDarkly open pull requests in the listed repositories, so confirm the schedule, repositories, and maxJobsPerRun with the user first. archival enabled false turns auto-archival off; an agent cannot turn it on: when it is off and enabled true is sent, nothing changes and the result gives the Automations page link for the user.

accountWide.description: true changes account settings and rejects repo, githubRepoId, and projectKey. false changes one repository and requires repo or githubRepoId.

approvalRequired.description: Whether auto-flagging pull requests need approval.

githubRepoId.description: Numeric GitHub repository id, an alternative to repo.

projectKey.description: Only when accountWide is false: the LaunchDarkly project to map the repository to. Required on the first map.

repo.description: GitHub repository as owner/name, for example launchdarkly/gonfalon.

name: delete-automations-repo-settings
description: Unmap a GitHub repository from Release Autopilot, removing its project mapping and overrides. Idempotent: an already-unmapped repository still succeeds. Pass repo as owner/name or githubRepoId.

githubRepoId.description: Numeric GitHub repository id, an alternative to repo.

projectKey.description: Any LaunchDarkly project key, used to look up the account-wide GitHub App install. Defaults to the oldest project.

repo.description: GitHub repository as owner/name, for example launchdarkly/gonfalon.

name: get-environment-release-plans
description: Get environment release plans, reusable progressive-release recipes. Without releasePlanKey: a page of plans, each marked default when it is the environment's default. With releasePlanKey: one plan.

environmentKey.description: Environment key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

offset.description: Only without releasePlanKey. Pass nextOffset from the previous page.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

releasePlanKey.description: Get one plan. Omit to list plans.

name: create-environment-release-plan
description: Create an environment release plan, a reusable progressive-release recipe. Does not start a release. Check existing plans with get-environment-release-plans first: an active key returns 409. PHASES: 1-10, each with 1-10 clauses and 1-10 steps. Every phase's clauses must include the randomization unit clause {attribute: "kind", op: "in", values: [<randomizationUnit>], contextKind: <randomizationUnit>}. STEPS: {allocation, durationMillis}; allocation is per-100k, greater than 0, at most 99000, increasing. Do not add a 100% step. METRICS: keyed object, each value { isGroup, autoRollback? }; {} = progressive.

environmentKey.description: Environment key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

metrics.description: Keyed by metric key. {} = progressive. Any key makes releases from this plan guarded. Each value is { isGroup, autoRollback? }.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

name: update-default-environment-release-plan
description: Set or clear an environment release plan as the environment's default, the plan suggested first when starting a release. default true makes this plan the default; default false clears it only when this plan is the default.

name: search-contexts
description: Search for stored LaunchDarkly contexts in an environment by kind, key, or attribute value. Returns context records including their stored attributes. kind filters to one context kind. filter uses `field operator value` clauses with operators equals, notEquals, anyOf, startsWith, exists, before, after; fields include kind, key, and <kind>.<attribute>, for example `user.email exists`.
